title: About
text:
The Democracy and Political Violence Collaborative convenes researchers who study democracy and political violence, across disciplines, subfields, career stages, and approaches. We hold a mini-conference every year at MPSA, host similar events at APSA and EPSS, and organize specific workshops and meetings. Beyond the paper sessions, our events are built to cultivate an enduring community of researchers, with dedicated time to connect, exchange ideas, and lay the groundwork for future collaboration.
Our first conference was a pre-conference to APSA 2026 at Harvard University. Our next is an MPSA 2027 Mini-Conference.

title: Democracy and Political ViolenceCollaborative
text:
About the Collaborative
The Democracy and Political Violence Collaborative brings together researchers who study democracy and political violence, broadly construed — regardless of discipline, subfield, career stage, or approach. This includes, but is not limited to, work on democratic resilience and backsliding, support for political violence and antidemocratic policies, and the effect of violence on political behavior.
Our goal is to provide a space for feedback, connection, and collaboration that bridges common divides, such as subfield and discipline. We hold a mini-conference every year at MPSA and host similar events at APSA and EPSS, along with specific workshops and meetings.

title: MPSA 2027 Mini-Conference
text:
Deadline: end of day, Monday, November 2, 2026 Decisions: by Friday, November 6, 2026
Apply or register interest
The Democracy and Political Violence Collaborative is hosting a mini-conference (a “conference within a conference”) during MPSA’s 2027 annual meeting on Saturday, April 3. This is our second meeting, following our pre-conference at APSA 2026.

title: MPSA 2027 Mini-Conference
text:
What we’re looking for
As always, we invite work — regardless of discipline, subfield, career stage, or approach — that studies democracy and political violence, broadly construed. This includes, but is not limited to, work on:

democratic resilience and backsliding
support for political violence and antidemocratic policies
the effect of violence on political behavior

We welcome submissions of all kinds, including abstracts, research plans, and papers.

title: MPSA 2027 Mini-Conference
text:
Format
The day will feature three paper panels, a roundtable on the state of the field and avenues for future research, and a reception and poster session. The rough schedule:

Coffee hour
Session 1
Session 2
Lunch
Session 3
Roundtable
Reception / poster session

While the conference focuses on accepted papers, attendance and discussion are open with advance registration. Beyond the paper sessions, the day is structured to build an enduring community of researchers in this space, with dedicated time for all attendees — presenters and non-presenters alike — to connect, exchange ideas, and lay the groundwork for future collaboration.
We expect all attendees to read the accepted papers, and accepted authors will also serve as discussants.

title: MPSA 2027 Mini-Conference
text:
How to apply
Use the application form to submit work or to register your interest in attending. The form requires a Google account to upload files.






NoteApplying to MPSA as well?



You can apply to present both at our mini-conference and at MPSA more generally. The two processes are separate: we handle submissions to the mini-conference directly, and general submissions are handled by MPSA.


Questions, or just want to connect? Reach out to the organizers.
